statement: An involution in the full three-cusp loop-outer group with 2-adic multiplier plus one has transposition puncture permutation and global multiplier plus one. The resulting multiplier character is therefore the usual global orientation character for finite subgroups with image positive S3, V4 with pure kernel, or full S3 times C2 under D32's faithful map.
where_proved: Part D, statement D.36; work/part_c/d36.tex; code/part_c/positive_transposition_d36.py
manuscript_passages: §30; folios194–196; scans383–387; §31; folios198–199verso; scans391–394; Part D(b) of the task
depends_on_doubtful_reading: None. The branched-puncture cyclic cover and the two-cusp filling are specified by exact group homomorphisms and presentations.
notes: The proof first extends the fixed-subgroup rank argument to actual pure finite-order automorphisms of genus-zero groups with any number of at least three cusps. A hypothetical negative odd-prime multiplier of a positive transposition gives a pure involution on the filled q-cusp cyclic cover, contradicting that lemma at2. It does not assume that arbitrary larger-rank outer actions have finite-order lifts. Negative transpositions, order-three actions, and geometric conjugacy remain outside the claimed conclusion.
